From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: marqué

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French marque. Doublet of mark. Ultimately cognate with marquee.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmɑː(ɹ)k/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɑː(ɹ)k
  • Homophones: mark, Mark

Noun

[edit]

marque (plural marques)

  2. A brand of a manufactured product, especially of a motor car.
    Synonym: make
    Hypernym: brand
    Coordinate term: model
    • 2001 January 31, Nicholas Bannister, “BMW's unofficial input into new MGs”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
      The group wants Rover as its luxury marque and MG as the performance car.
    • 2020 December 3, Brett Berk, “The S.U.V.-ification of Everything Comes to Classic British Marques”, in The New York Times‎[2], →ISSN:
      And there seems to be an intrinsic disconnect between a high-end marque and the utilitarian nature of an S.U.V.
  4. A license to pass the limits of a jurisdiction, or boundary of a country, for the purpose of making reprisals or privateering; the document recording this license.
    Synonyms: letter of marque, letter of marque and reprisal
  6. A ship commissioned for making captures.
    Synonym: letter of marque

Derived terms

[edit]
  • countermarque
  • letter of marque and reprisal

Translations

[edit]
brand of a manufactured product
  • Finnish: merkki (fi)
  • French: marque (fr) f
  • German: Marke (de) f
  • Vietnamese: nhãn hiệu (vi), mác (vi)

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Middle French marquer
Middle French marque
French marque

    From Middle French marque (15th c.), deverbal from marquer, which see for more. Related with marc (“a weight”), mark (“a currency”), marche (“frontier”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /maʁk/
    • Audio:(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
    • Rhymes: -aʁk
    • Homophones: Marc, mark, marks, marques (general), marc, marcs (one pronunciation)

    Noun

    [edit]

    marque f (plural marques)

    1. mark (spot)
    2. brand (of a company)
    3. mark (on one's body, e.g. a birthmark)

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • à vos marques, prêts, partez
    • hôte de marque
    • image de marque
    • marque commerciale
    • marque de fabrique
    • marque déposée
    • marque-page
    • marquer
    • nom de marque
    • ouvrir la marque
    • prendre ses marques
    • trouver ses marques

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • → Egyptian Arabic: مرك (mark)
    • → English: marque
    • → German: Marke
      • → Belarusian: ма́рка (márka)
      • → Bulgarian: ма́рка (márka)
      • → Kashubian: merk
      • → Macedonian: ма́рка (márka)
      • → Russian: ма́рка (márka)
      • → Ukrainian: ма́рка (márka)
      • → Yiddish: מאַרקע (marke)
    • → Persian: مارک (mârk)

    See also

    [edit]
    • signe

    marque

    1. inflection of marquer:
      1. first/third-person singular present indicative/subjunctive
      2. second-person singular imperative
